title: Does the form of compensation matter?

rival_explanations: banker reputation (cross-correlated with bidder managerial ownership) rather than ownership drives total-value fee use
bidder managerial ownership (cross-correlated with reputation) rather than reputation drives contract choice

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (tender offers / investment banking in the market for corporate control)
context.sample_description: Tender offers for NYSE-listed target firms; primary data on fee contracts from SEC Schedule 14D filings; offers compiled from the SEC News Digest, with announcement/outcome data from the Wall Street Journal and target-firm ownership from Value Line; fixed-fee contracts excluded
context.sample_size: 161 target-firm and 241 bidding-firm observations (reduced to 148 and 227 after eliminating fixed-fee contracts)

data_sources.name: Schedule 14D filings (Schedule 14D1 and 14D9) required by the SEC
Wall Street Journal and Wall Street Journal Index
Carter and Manaster (1990) underwriter reputation rankings

dv.name: offer outcome measures and excess fees compared across contract types
dv.measure: Univariate comparisons of explanatory variables and outcome measures across contract types; chi-square tests of joint frequencies (Panel A) and F-tests of continuous variables (Panel B); excess fees estimated from residuals of a regression of ln(fee) on ln(offer value)
dv.source: Wall Street Journal and Wall Street Journal Index
